summary: Amended a 1905 order on Fort St. Michael, Alaska, so that all reservation land except a described military tract would pass to the Interior Department for disposal, effective November 1, 1907.
Let the officer in charge of Public Buildings and Grounds hire a copyist for up to three months to help with an inventory.

Allowed the Civil Service Commission, when too few American citizens qualified for posts such as interpreter, to accept non-citizen applicants, certifying them only when no eligible citizens remained.
Pushed back the abolition of the Surveyor General's office for Florida, ordered in April 1906, from June 30, 1906, to June 30, 1907.
Removed certain tracts from a 1904 land withdrawal in the Hailey Land District, Idaho, so they could be used for town sites under an April 1906 act.
Cleared the way for Dr. Cressy L. Wilbur, an expert special agent, to move up to chief statistician for vital statistics at the Bureau of the Census.
Changed the civil-service rules so temporary forest guards, unlike other seasonal fire-season workers, were no longer limited to six months of work a year.
Made Saturdays in July, August and September four-hour workdays for mechanics, laborers and classified employees at the Washington navy yard, with time-and-a-half for extra hours.
Reserved land within the Belle Fourche irrigation project in South Dakota for agricultural experiment work.
Required civil-service examinations for certain internal revenue positions in North Carolina's fifth district that were exempt elsewhere.
Withdrew all unappropriated public lands in Wisconsin north of Township 33 from entry, settlement or other claims for 90 days.
Set four-hour Saturdays for skilled mechanics, laborers and classified workers at the Government Printing Office in July, August and September, paying time-and-a-half for longer shifts.
Let Everett J. Dallas, a Civil War veteran, move from an "additional" seat on the board of pension appeals to a regular, competitive seat as the extra posts were cut.
Kept Col. O. H. Ernst on as a member of the International Waterways Commission.
Enlarged the Lincoln Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory to take in additional land partly covered with timber.
Created the San Luis Obispo Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in California.
Established the Monterey Forest Reserve from partly timbered public lands in California.
Extended summer four-hour Saturdays to skilled mechanics, laborers and classified employees at every U.S. navy yard and naval station, with time-and-a-half for extra hours.
Set merit rules for the newly reorganized consular service: top consular posts filled by promotion for ability and efficiency, and entry-level consul posts by promotion or by examination.
Gave War Department arsenal, depot and Army headquarters workers four-hour Saturdays during July, August and September.
Permitted one more special pension examiner to be hired for six months outside the civil-service rules, on top of five already excepted.
Allowed Mrs. Emma King (née Anderson) to return to the Bureau of Engraving and Printing even though more than a year had passed since she left.
Appointed James K. Dawes a clerk at $1,200 a year in the Philadelphia post office, waiving the usual civil-service eligibility rules.
Expanded the Black Mesa Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory by changing its boundaries to add land.
Moved Charles N. Twadell from an exam-exempt special examiner job in the Bureau of Pensions to a similar post under the regular rules.
Fixed salaries for the Isthmian Canal Commission, from $30,000 for Chairman Theodore P. Shonts to $7,500 for three commissioners, and set rules for housing and travel expenses.
Directed the Civil Service Commission to give honorably discharged Navy and military men preference for fireman, engineer and similar jobs in the State, War, and Navy Department building.
Let Ralph Modjeski be appointed consulting engineer at Rock Island Arsenal, after a noncompetitive exam, while the Rock Island bridge and viaduct were built.
Redrew the boundaries of the Fort Bayard military reservation in New Mexico to match General Land Office plats, adding a narrow strip of public land on the west side.
Allowed William E. De Riemer, who had spent about seven years on National Museum exposition work, to be hired as a Smithsonian clerk at up to $900 a year.
Brought four Smithsonian employees working on the International Catalogue of Scientific Literature into the classified service, with future hires for that work made under civil-service rules.
Classified Bureau of Fisheries field laborers doing fish-culture work, letting them be transferred and promoted under civil-service rules.
Allowed clerical jobs on the Isthmus of Panama paying $75 a month or less to be filled without examination, and let clerks hired by mistake under a January 1906 order become permanent.
Set apart the Pinnacles Forest Reserve on public lands in California.
Created the Heppner Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.
Ordered that applications to enter newly opened Shoshone (Wind River) Reservation lands be filed at Shoshoni, Wyoming, instead of Lander, through October 3, 1906.
Let Michael J. Holland, an enlisted Marine, be appointed a clerk at Marine Corps headquarters.
Cut land out of the Malabang military reservation on Mindanao, Philippine Islands, for the newly organized municipality of Malabang.
Extended by ten years the trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac and Fox and Iowa Indians.
Set four-hour Saturdays in July, August and September for mechanics, laborers and other workers in the War Department's Engineer Department at Large.
Granted Office of Public Buildings and Grounds employees, except the Park Police, paid Saturday half-holidays in July, August and September, with conditions for temporary workers.
Permitted Miss Elizabeth Stack to be appointed to a clerical job in the Pension Office without a civil-service exam.
Turned certain California lands, previously reserved for military use, over to naval purposes.
Let Tony Verrosso, a Spanish-American War veteran, be hired as an unclassified laborer out of the usual certification order.
Allowed Mrs. Florence E. Broady a permanent Government Printing Office appointment without a civil-service exam.
Moved part of the El Reno Land District in Oklahoma into the Lawton Land District.
Authorized Mrs. Julia Lynah McCoy's appointment to a Treasury Department position without a civil-service exam.
Redrew the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, adding some timbered land, dropping other tracts and restoring those to settlement.
Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's authority to January 1, 1907, and no longer, so it could finish judging U.S. citizens' claims against Spain.
Set apart the Crazy Mountains Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.
Renamed the Board on Geographic Names the United States Geographic Board and gave it advisory power over federal mapmaking, including avoiding duplicate work and standardizing scales and symbols.
Established the Kootenai Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Montana.
Moved the headquarters of the Coeur d'Alene Indian Agency to Tekoa.
Amended the regulations governing the U.S. consular service.
Set a new tariff of fees for U.S. consular services, effective November 1, 1906, payable in gold, with American vessels and seamen exempt by law.
Let W. M. Johnson be appointed in the Immigration Service without a civil-service exam.
Allowed E. J. Mooklar to be reinstated as clerk to the commandant of the naval station at Tutuila, Samoa, despite the one-year reinstatement limit.
Created the Wasatch Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Utah.
Let Everett Spring join the Bureau of the Census without an exam, based on his earlier work as a census clerk and local special agent.
Set apart the Goose Lake Forest Reserve on public lands in Oregon.
Called on Americans to help the earthquake victims of Valparaiso, Chile, recalling the world's help to San Francisco that spring, and pointed donors to the National Red Cross.
Lowered U.S. duties on certain Spanish products after Spain gave American goods its minimum tariff rates starting September 1, 1906.
Extended for ten years the trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac and Fox and Iowa Indians.
Excused Washington Navy Yard employees from work on Labor Day, September 3, 1906.
Restored two small lots in the former Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, to the public domain after they were mistakenly included in David Eskelson's homestead.
Added partly timbered land in California to the Stanislaus Forest Reserve.
Permitted Miss Alice A. Masters to be appointed a Census Bureau clerk without a civil-service exam.
Further enlarged the Hell Gate Forest Reserve in Montana with additional partly timbered land.

Handed part of the Fort Robinson military reservation, Nebraska, to the Interior Department for disposal, since it was useless for military purposes and had been mistakenly included in private patents.
Reduced U.S. duties on certain Bulgarian goods after Bulgaria granted American products its lowest conventional tariff rates.
Set apart the Fremont Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.
Combined the Tahoe and Yuba forest reserves, with added land, into a single Tahoe Forest Reserve in California and Nevada.
Authorized extra pay for enlisted Marines detailed as messmen.

Opened to settlement the 480,000 acres of grazing land and the wood reserve in the Kiowa, Comanche and Apache reservations, Oklahoma Territory, except tracts allotted, sold or set aside for town sites.

summary: Told federal departments overseeing public works to report every case of contractors working laborers or mechanics more than eight hours in a day.
Created the Lolo Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.
Moved Julius H. Hammond, a General Land Office depositary and confidential clerk, into the competitive classified service along with his position.
Rescheduled the Isthmian Canal Commission's quarterly session from October 1 to November 15, 1906, at the Canal Zone governor's office in Panama.
Enlarged the Shasta Forest Reserve in California with additional partly timbered land.
Set apart the Long Pine Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.
Declared Devils Tower in Crook County, Wyoming, a national monument under the new Antiquities Act, calling the lofty, isolated rock "a natural wonder" and warning against injuring it.
Opened unallotted, unreserved lands of the Walker River Indian Reservation in Nevada, ceded by the Pah Ute Indians, to settlement at noon on October 29, 1906.
Allowed Joseph Tyssowski, valued for his knowledge of public land law, to be reinstated in the Interior Department despite the time limit.
Exempted one private secretary in the naval officer of customs' office at the port of New York from civil-service examination.
Extended Navy prizes for excellence in gunnery and target practice, afloat and ashore, to enlisted Marines on the same terms, for competitions after June 30, 1906.
Approved moving the Surveyor General of Alaska's office from Sitka to Juneau.
Expanded the Santa Barbara Forest Reserve in California to take in additional partly timbered land.
Gave members of the United Spanish War Veterans working in Washington's federal departments, printing office and navy yard the day off October 9, 1906, to march in the group's parade.
Carved the Iloilo port light site, mistakenly included in the Fort San Pedro military reservation on Panay, Philippine Islands, out of that reservation.
Created the Siskiyou Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.
Set apart the Mount Taylor Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in New Mexico Territory.
Let Joe Osscar stay on as engineer at the Leech Lake Indian Agency in Minnesota without a civil-service exam.
Excused members of the Grand Army of the Republic working in the executive departments at Washington from duty for the Spanish War Veterans' parade.
Added more partly timbered land in Utah to the Uinta Forest Reserve, which spans Utah and Wyoming.
Made part of the Fort Grant military reservation in Arizona part of the Mt. Graham Forest Reserve, while keeping it open to unhampered War Department use and closed to land-law claims.
